text.p: Italian bonds and futures slid sharply by the close of trade as the falling Bund market managed to take Btps with it.
Brokers said the tumble triggered big stop losses, shoving the Btp market lower still.

"There's maybe some disappointment the Bank of Italy hasn't lowered interest rates but the market has also lost two points in as many days and so people are closing out long positions," a London-based futures broker said.
The June contract on LIFFE was 97 basis points down at 129.48 with support plotted at 129.00/05 and then 128.30.
The February 2007 Btp ended 68 basis points down at 96.92, with the yield at 7.31 percent and the spread over the benchmark Bund creeping out to 139 basis points from 136 earlier.

Dealers noted the Btp-Bund spread hugged record lows for much of the day although it later widened a few basis points. But one pointed out: "The volumes on our markets are relatively low, 70,000 lots on LIFFE in respect to more than 300,000 in Bunds and 134,000 in Spanish Bonos. That's a comforting signal."
They said the sales might also be due to a long weekend in the UK, with no one wanting to go home long on Friday ahead of the first round of French elections this weekend.
Brokers also noted the lira was holding steady against the mark and there was no particular domestic news to jog prices.

Earlier, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he saw the signs of economic recovery and added that Italy's budget deficit to gross domestic product ratio was already at the magic three percent required for joining a single European currency.

Prodi also said all the conditions were there for Italy to be a founding member of EMU. However an IMF official, in a magazine interview, urged Italy to define and implement crucial pension reforms along with the 1998 budget.
